beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Jesus told this story to religious leaders — people who were sure they had already said yes to God. He told it so they would hear themselves in it.

He told it so they would hear themselves in it.
The first answer was blunt.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The answer from the other son sounded much better.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The promise sounded respectful, but it never became obedience.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The first son meant his no. But it wouldn't leave him alone. All morning, the vineyard kept pulling at him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So he got up. And he went. No announcement, no apology. He went back to the vineyard, and he worked.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The row the second son promised to work stayed empty all day. Then Jesus asked the crowd a question.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Whether of them twain did the will of his father?

timing.text: Whether of them twain did the will of his father?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The difference was not what the sons said; it was what they finally did. The crowd knew the answer.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their answer condemned their own confidence. The son who began in rebellion had changed direction; the polite son had not. Then Jesus turned to the religious leaders — the ones who were sure they were the second son.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.

card.text: Have you ever said no to something — maybe loudly — and found yourself moving toward it anyway, because part of you couldn't let it go?
